title: Issue the Ed25519 rizzstack.ticket/1 JWS from the coordinator

outcome.summary: bundlebees_plugin/ticket.py mints the compact JWS that hyvv ADR 0002 puts at the dispatch boundary. Given a validated brief, an injected 32-byte Ed25519 seed, a kid and an audience, issue_ticket returns base64url(header).base64url(payload).base64url(signature) with header exactly {alg: EdDSA, kid}; the signed payload is the RFC 8785 (JCS) form of the twelve rizzstack.ticket/1 claims. brief_sha256 hashes the JCS form of the brief with its ticket key removed, assigned_files_sha256 hashes the JCS form of assigned_files, contract_sha256 hashes the embedded contract object or is null. exp is exactly iat + 600 and no caller can mint a longer ticket. jti is 32 lower-case hex, fresh per issue and single-use through an in-memory JtiLedger. The private key is a required caller argument: the module never reads the environment, the home directory or a key file, so the coordinator's secret store stays outside the library. cryptography is an optional 'tickets' extra; importing the module without it succeeds and issuing fails closed with the named TicketCryptoUnavailable.
observable_behavior: issue_ticket(brief, *, private_key, kid, audience, now=None, jti=None, ledger=None, ttl_seconds=600) returns a three-part compact JWS whose header is exactly {"alg": "EdDSA", "kid": kid}.
The payload decodes to exactly the twelve ADR claims and its bytes are the JCS canonical JSON of those claims; the signature verifies over header.payload with the matching public key.
brief_sha256 is SHA-256 of the JCS form of the brief without its ticket key: key order and a stale ticket on the input cannot change it, and a changed brief does.
assigned_files_sha256 and contract_sha256 are SHA-256 of the JCS forms of assigned_files and the embedded contract object; a brief without a contract records null.
iat is the supplied now (or wall clock), exp is iat + 600, TICKET_TTL_SECONDS is 600 and ttl_seconds above 600 raises TicketError.
jti is 32 lower-case hex, differs across issues, and a JtiLedger refuses a second claim of the same jti with TicketReuseError.

issue_ticket requires private_key as a keyword-only argument with no default; the module source has no os.environ/getenv/Path.home/expanduser access and opens no key path even when candidate BUNDLEBEES_*/RIZZSTACK_*/COORDINATOR_* key variables point at one.

cryptography is not a core dependency: pyproject declares it under the optional 'tickets' extra; with the import blocked the module still loads and issue_ticket raises TicketCryptoUnavailable naming cryptography, never a bare ImportError.

interfaces.name: bundlebees_plugin.ticket.issue_ticket
interfaces.notes: issue_ticket(brief: Mapping, *, private_key: bytes, kid: str, audience: str, now: int | None = None, jti: str | None = None, ledger: JtiLedger | None = None, ttl_seconds: int = TICKET_TTL_SECONDS) -> str. Builds the twelve claims, JCS-canonicalises them and signs header.payload with Ed25519. No I/O beyond the caller-supplied values.

interfaces.name: bundlebees_plugin.ticket.JtiLedger
interfaces.notes: In-memory single-use jti ledger: claim(jti, exp) raises TicketReuseError on a second claim; the issuer consults it when one is supplied.

interfaces.name: bundlebees_plugin.ticket.brief_digest
interfaces.notes: SHA-256 hex of the RFC 8785 canonical JSON of the brief without its ticket key.

interfaces.name: bundlebees_plugin.ticket.TicketError
interfaces.notes: Base refusal type; TicketReuseError and TicketCryptoUnavailable derive from it and are importable without cryptography.

interfaces.name: pyproject.toml
interfaces.notes: Add optional-dependencies.tickets carrying cryptography; the core dependencies list stays free of it.

acceptance_criteria.statement: the issued JWS has the EdDSA header, decodes to exactly the twelve ADR claims and verifies with the test public key
brief_sha256 is the RFC 8785 digest of the brief minus ticket, stable under key order and a stale ticket
exp is exactly iat + 600 seconds and a longer requested lifetime is refused
jti is random 32-hex and single use: a second claim of the same jti is refused
the private key is injected, the module never consults env/home/key paths, and no key material is committed
cryptography is an optional extra and a missing import fails closed with the named TicketCryptoUnavailable
empty audience/kid and a brief without a risk tier are refused, and a fixed key/jti/iat issues byte-identical JWS

dependencies: wave-c-C1: the twelve claims and their types are the rizzstack.ticket/1 schema frozen in workflow
owner answer 2026-11-25: signing is an optional extra, the private key lives in the coordinator's secret store and production key generation waits for the owner
assumptions: private_key is the coordinator's raw 32-byte Ed25519 seed from its secret store; loading that secret is the caller's job and is not implemented in this slice
the tests carry their own Ed25519 verifier and RFC 8785 canonicalizer so the issuer is checked independently; wave D may land a shared JCS core later without changing these behaviours
only throwaway keys generated at test time are used; no production key, key file or key material enters the repository
JtiLedger is an in-process guard against double issuance within one coordinator; the cross-process, cross-restart single-use guarantee is C4's on-disk ReplayCache.

r1 diagnosis (att_ee69117be8ad4992, green_failed): 10 of the 18 approved cases raised TicketCryptoUnavailable because the verification interpreter (verify_python /var/tmp/bundlebees-py, CPython 3.12) has no cryptography, and the Hermes CPython 3.14 venv carries cryptography 50.0.2 whose Ed25519 binding raises ModuleNotFoundError: _cffi_backend. The r1 patch is behaviourally correct: the identical diff passes 18/18 wherever the tickets extra imports (proven with uv run --with cryptography).

GREEN requires the tickets extra pre-provisioned in the verification interpreter: the verify sandbox runs offline (--net=none) and no test may install anything at run time, so cryptography is installed into verify_python on the host before tdd red and verify.

reasons: the issuer is the only component that touches the coordinator signing key; a leak or an implicit key discovery would let anyone mint tickets
the ticket becomes the admission credential for every hyvv create in wave C
introduces the first cryptography dependency path in bundlebees, even as an optional extra
risk.blast_radius: wave C tickets, preflight and every dispatch that later presents a ticket
